_README: Runtime import exemptions enforced by isoexec/checks/lint.py.
Categories a (external numerics) and b (monkeypatch debt) may only shrink; adding debt requires updating the ownership design.
Category c covers runtime plumbing and registration; gate covers tests comparing with upstream implementations.
Remove an exemption when its import disappears. Core, nn, and schema permit no runtime-import exemptions.
Prefixes match normalized dotted import targets at a dot boundary, including statically resolvable importlib calls.

exemptions.reason: Engine attention-context accessor used by the registered backend. Plumbing for the same registration.
Registers a CUSTOM vLLM attention backend. Subclassing the engine's backend/metadata types IS the registration interface; `vllm.v1.attention.backends.*` is named plumbing in §2c. Engine-side only.

The KV-cache layout enum the CUSTOM backend names in supported_kv_cache_layouts(), so vLLM allocates pages the arch-selected GQA kernel reads in place. Plumbing for the same registration. Engine-side only.

INVERTED direction, and the two live imports are the only ones left in ops/gdn/shared/ after kernel-ownership.md §5.4 vendored the FLA kernels into ops/gdn/shared/vendored_fla. Neither can be vendored away, because neither reads upstream numerics -- both WRITE ours into vLLM's modules. (1) pin_gdn_rmsnorm_rows_per_block rebinds `fla.ops.layernorm_guard.calc_rows_per_block` to a constant so vLLM's own RMSNormGated (layers.layernorm.RMSNormGated.forward_cuda -> layernorm_guard.rmsnorm_fn) stops sizing its fp32 tile from the row count; the engine keeps that norm, only _forward_core is rebound. (2) _import_upstream pins vLLM's copies of the nine autotuned FLA kernels to the same config index as ours, because QwenGatedDeltaNetAttention._warmup_prefill_kernels still launches them during V1 profiling and our _forward_core rebind does not reach it. A copy of either would pin nothing.
vLLM's sleep/wake memory allocator. Memory plumbing, explicitly named in kernel-ownership.md §2c.
vLLM GPU worker lifecycle hook for sleep/wake. Process plumbing, named in kernel-ownership.md §2c.

Gate test: imports the upstream kernel in order to prove ours equals it bitwise. This is the vendoring discipline, not a violation of it -- after the kernel is vendored this import is the only thing keeping the copy honest, so it stays. Parity of our native GDN kernels against vLLM's FLA -- exactly the gate §5.4 will need.

Wraps mcore's activation-checkpoint callable (and its RNG-state machinery in tensor_parallel.random) so a recompute re-enters OUR triton kernel instead of torch.matmul. This installs our numerics onto the trainer's control flow; it borrows none of mcore's. Fail-closed: returns False and declines to install if mcore is absent, and the caller then installs the unscoped kernel -- same forward, so no impl-id change.

Gate test: imports the upstream kernel in order to prove ours equals it bitwise. This is the vendoring discipline, not a violation of it -- after the kernel is vendored this import is the only thing keeping the copy honest, so it stays. Gates the forward-only bmm scope against vLLM's kernel.

Gate test, of the class check 8 exists for: it imports the pinned wheel's own `FlashAttentionBackend` / `FlashAttentionMetadataBuilder` / `AttentionCGSupport` / `AttentionBackendEnum` in order to assert that the three class facts the CUSTOM backend owes vLLM are still what the WHEEL says -- `forward_includes_kv_cache_update=False` and `supports_batch_invariance()->True` are INHERITED, and re-declaring them on our side to avoid this import is exactly the failure mode the test exists to prevent (our copy would then agree with itself forever). Assertions only: nothing here builds a backend, allocates, or runs a kernel.
Gate test: asserts the CUSTOM backend's declared KV-cache layouts are the pinned wheel's own enum members. Assertions only.
